text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: kv-cache continuous-batching regression on llm-serving-prod cluster (region: us-west-2). latency p95 jump from 120ms -> 1.8s, 503s increasing. Top affected model tags: llama-2-13b, qwen-14b.
alice: ack, I'm oncall. paging eng-runtime and eng-ml. linking logs and graphs: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/kv/kv-cache?panel=65
sophie: seeing this too, just rolled out a batch-config change at 2026-03-15T03:02UTC (canary->prod) that adjusted `max_batch_window_ms` from 20 -> 80 and `prefetch_factor` +0.25. Was intended to improve throughput on small-context requests.
alice: @sophie can you confirm the rollout id? we might need to rollback quickly.
sophie: rollout id r2026-03-15-0819, 30% then 100% in 10m. I can pause/rollback.
opsbot: Automated alert: kv_kvcache_prefix_cardinality metric spiked by 420% in 10m; eviction_latency up 5x.
mike: customer impact: AcmePayments reported transaction timeouts (~3% of requests) and a support ticket opened. Customer region: us-west.
bob: logs show KV cache growth per-prefix: many tiny prefixes from payment IDs. Continuous batching is coalescing too aggressively, causing `kv_work_queue` backlog and blocking hot-path threads. Example trace:
```
I0315 03:09:21.123 worker.cc:412] prefix=acct_12345 delta_kv=+12 cache_size=1.4GB backlog=342 queue_delay_ms=420
```
carol: probable root cause: wider batch window + increased prefetch allowed more speculative prefixes to be fetched/retained, increasing prefix cardinality and preventing timely eviction. Model behaviors: llama requests have many short-latency prefixes (GQA) while qwen requests cause larger KV entries (MQA) — both amplified by the config.
alice: plan: 1) pause/rollback rollout to r2026-03-15-0818 (previous stable) 2) reduce max_batch_window_ms to 15 and prefetch_factor to 0.0 globally for critical clusters 3) bump eviction thresholds transiently and flush caches on warm nodes 4) notify Acme and enable fallbacks to smaller model variants.
sophie: doing rollback now.
deploy-bot: deploy rollback r2026-03-15-0819 -> r2026-03-15-0818 triggered by @sophie (id: rollback-3740001111). Rolling back batch-config map `kv-batch-config/llm-serving-prod`.
opsbot: Rolling update started, 120 nodes to update, concurrency 10.
mike: @alice please trigger temporary model fallback rule so Acme gets qwen-small instead of qwen-14b (reduces KV pressure).
alice: done: added routing policy rule `fallback: qwen-14b -> qwen-7b` for tenant AcmePayments (policy-id pf-374-acy). Monitoring.
carol: while rollback is in progress, we should hotpatch eviction threshold on pods to free memory quicker. patch snippet:
```
kubectl -n prod set env deployment/llm-worker KV_MAX_PREFIX_BYTES=25000000 KV_EVICT_INTERVAL_MS=500
```
bob: applying patch to a subset first (canary 10 pods) then bulk.
sophie: rollback completed on config maps at 03:18UTC; rollout of previous config confirmed.
opsbot: Rolling update completed 120/120 nodes (duration 6m).
alice: observed p95 drop to 210ms within 2 minutes, 503s down to baseline. kv_prefix_cardinality trending down.
mike: AcmePayments ops notified: "We saw a transient outage — mitigation in place, rolling back config; we'll follow up with postmortem." they asked for timeframe and SLA credits; forwarding to CS.
carol: post-mitigation follow-ups: - add model-specific batch profiles (llama/gqa vs qwen/mqa) - telemetry to track prefix_cardinality per-tenant - add canary gate: require KV prefix_cardinality delta < 50% to progress from 30%->100% rollout - auto-fallback when eviction_latency > 2s
alice: agreed. assigning actions: @carol (runbook + postmortem), @sophie (improve rollout gating), @bob (add eviction autoscale), @mike (customer comms + SLA touchpoint).
incident-bot: Incident severity set to P1 -> mitigated. start_time=3740001111, mitigated_time=3740001250, owner=alice.
sophie: one more note: the config change was flagged in PERF lab but didn't hit production telemetry thresholds because the lab workload lacked high prefix-cardinality patterns (payments). will add synthetic prefix-card tests.
alice: handing off to @mike for next shift summary and follow-ups. brief handoff:
- root cause: batch window expansion + prefetch increases caused KV prefix cardinality explosion under payment traffic patterns -> eviction lag -> request latency + 503s
- mitigation: rollback to previous batch config, reduce batch window, patch eviction env to be more aggressive, set tenant fallback to smaller model
- customer impact: AcmePayments ~3% timeouts for ~20m window, ticket created #INC-4521
- next steps: model-specific batch profiles, rollout gating on prefix_cardinality, add synthetic telemetry test
mike: taking handoff. Will open follow-up tickets, schedule postmortem meeting tomorrow 10am PT, and draft customer follow-up.
alice: thanks team. marking incident thread closed for oncall. :thumbsup:
carol: FYI we'll need to run a short load test to validate new gating rules once implemented. I'll attach test harness.
mike: handed off to next oncall in slack: @mike -> @sophie (next shift). closing.
